trust_decision.summary: Each archive member's host destination is decided by lexically joining its (dot-dot-filtered) name onto the rootfs/container dir, with no check that intermediate path components are not symlinks planted by earlier members; the fix adds per-hop clamped symlink resolution (_safe_resolve) at every write/read site.

landing_point.why: Summary names `proot-distro install` + malicious tar; install_local.extract_plain_tar and docker layers.apply_layer both delegate to extract_tar_to_rootfs, whose _process_member builds parent/dest by plain os.path.join.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `proot-distro install` (local tar / URL / docker pull / local OCI via apply_layer)
CLI `proot-distro install` (dir member onto an existing symlink)
CLI `proot-distro install` (deferred hardlink copy, both endpoints)

fix_sites.module_kind: second implementation (separate streaming extractor in commands/)

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `proot-distro build` (Dockerfile COPY/ADD, incl. ADD auto-extracted tar)
fix_sites.module_kind: build engine step (third materialiser, file_map based)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: proot_distro/commands/restore.py:268-355 (own tar loop, not using tar_extract) and proot_distro/helpers/build_engine/copy_step.py:432-479 (file_map materialiser for `build`)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Advisory says `install`; restore only accepts archives 'created by proot-distro backup' (restore.py:263-265) and build's COPY/ADD inputs come from the user's own Dockerfile/context, so a solver can argue neither ingests attacker archives.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate symlinks in images (merged-usr `lib -> usr/lib`, absolute `/var/run -> /run`) must still be followed, re-rooted at the rootfs, so later layers/members writing through them land inside the rootfs; an over-broad fix that skips or rejects any member whose parent is a symlink breaks layered OCI installs, restore of normal backups and COPY into such paths.

O6_input_shapes: symlink member with absolute target (`evil -> /`) then a file member written through it
symlink member with relative ascending target (`evil -> ../../`) then a file member through it
directory member whose name is already an existing symlink (makedirs/chmod follow it)
hardlink whose linkname routes through a planted symlink (host file read into rootfs)
hardlink member processed before the symlink that redirects it (deferred copy re-resolved at copy time)
symlink loops / excessive chains (return None, skip member)
restore: new `<name>/rootfs/...` layout, legacy `installed-rootfs/<name>/...` layout and `<name>/<other>` back-compat layout, all resolved relative to container_dir
build: file_map arcnames from ADD-extracted tar, context directory trees with symlinks, and COPY --from stage

O8_uncovered_routes.route: install post-extraction fixups write/append/chmod etc/resolv.conf, etc/hosts, etc/passwd|shadow|group|gshadow via raw os.path.join, following an archive-planted `etc` symlink on the host (the fix deliberately leaves such symlinks on disk).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fixups write fixed, trusted content to fixed paths after extraction, not archive data; write_hosts already unlinks the final component (proot_distro/helpers/rootfs.py:53-60), so it looks handled.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: build engine also runs write_resolv_conf/write_hosts on stage rootfs assembled from pulled layers.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Build is a separate command; base images are 'trusted' by the Dockerfile author.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: login (crossing install->login state) chmods rootfs/tmp to 01777 and writes etc/profile.d/termux-profile.sh via raw joins, following a `tmp` or `etc` symlink planted by the installed archive.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Login is a different command that runs after install; the advisory is about extraction.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: restore deferred dir-mode chmod: a dir with a mode lacking owner rwx is queued, then a later member replaces it with a symlink, and the final os.chmod follows it to a host path (fix clamps only the parent at queue time).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fixed site's _safe_dest already ran on that path; deferred chmod looks like cosmetic mode restoration.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as fix, 60 lines below; final loop at proot_distro/commands/restore.py:365-369

O8_uncovered_routes.route: tar_extract deferred directory utime follows a symlink that a later member put in place of the directory (timestamps only).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only mtime is changed; low impact.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: build _materialise_files dir-kind entry: makedirs(exist_ok)+chmod on a final component that is an existing symlink (from base image/earlier layer) follows it to the host; fix clamps the parent only and does not add the islink drop it added in tar_extract.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The published fix already touched this function; final-component handling looks deliberate ('never a same-named symlink's target').

O8_uncovered_routes.route: COPY --from=<stage|image> source check is lexical only; a symlinked component in the source stage rootfs makes the read follow to a host file that is packed into the layer (same read-side issue the fix clamped for hardlink sources).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Read side, Dockerfile-author-controlled path, and the advisory is about writes.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: WORKDIR makedirs+chmod 0755 on raw-joined host path follows base-image symlinks out of the stage rootfs.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Path is from the Dockerfile author, not an archive.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: copy/sync `name:path` specs are contained lexically only (normpath+startswith), so guest symlinks in the path redirect host-side writes outside the rootfs.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: User-invoked copy between host and container; not archive extraction (borderline for the advisory's property).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: top-level paths.py, used by proot_distro/commands/copy.py:54-117 and proot_distro/commands/sync.py:406-501

O8b_injection_room.sibling: another post-install fixup (e.g. etc/machine-id or etc/timezone writer) using os.path.join(rootfs, 'etc', ...)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module exists to hold such Termux integration fixups and is reused by other entry points (rootfs.py:21-25).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: whiteout handler that resolves the whited-out sibling's path by following the final component
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: OCI whiteouts are handled ad hoc in the same extractor; a maintainer extending opaque-dir handling could easily join paths naively.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: restore post-step that rewrites manifest.json or applies rootfs fixups after extraction
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: install already writes manifest + fixups; parity for restore is a natural feature.
